item.title: Where are BTL landlords securing the strongest rental returns?
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
By Bambang Setiawan

Buy-to-let landlords across England are seeing varying rental yields, with northern cities and certain regional markets offering particularly strong returns, according to recent analysis. The Letting Partnership’s research reveals that the average nominal rental yield in England stands at 5.9%, based on an average property price of £293,262 and monthly rent of £1,446. However, some areas are delivering yields close to 7%, making them attractive options for property investors.

Top performers for rental yields

Newcastle upon Tyne leads the way with an estimated gross rental yield of 6.9%, underpinned by an average property price of £208,589 and monthly rent of £1,206. Close behind are Portsmouth and Manchester, both achieving yields of 6.5%. Southampton and Tower Hamlets in London follow with yields of 6.4%, while Bristol, Blackpool, and Nottingham each offer returns of 6.3%. Lincoln and Kingston upon Hull round out the list with yields of 6.2%.

These figures highlight the importance of location when it comes to buy-to-let investments. While property prices in these areas may be lower than in London and the South East, the rental yields they generate often outpace those in more expensive markets.

London’s contrasting picture

In contrast, London boroughs such as Westminster and Kensington and Chelsea demonstrate significantly lower yields, despite their high rental incomes. Westminster, for example, boasts an average monthly rent of £3,168 but delivers an estimated yield of just 4.5%. Similarly, Kensington and Chelsea’s average rent of £3,596 results in a yield of only 3.5%.

While these areas generate substantial annual rental incomes—£38,000 in Westminster and £43,000 in Kensington and Chelsea—their lower yields reflect the premium property prices in these boroughs. This stark difference underscores the trade-off between rental income and property value, which landlords might consider when choosing where to invest.

Regional opportunities for landlords

The research suggests that regional markets, particularly in the North of England, continue to offer some of the most favourable conditions for buy-to-let investors. These areas combine relatively affordable property prices with strong rental demand, resulting in higher yields. For landlords looking to maximise returns, exploring opportunities outside of London could prove beneficial.

Chris Mason, COO of The Letting Partnership, commented: “Yield is understandably front of mind for landlords, and, as the figures show, there are still parts of the country where investors can achieve very healthy returns.”

Ultimately, the choice of location depends on individual investment goals. While some landlords may prioritise high rental yields, others might focus on areas with long-term capital growth potential. Careful research and consideration of market trends could help investors make informed decisions that align with their financial objectives.

item.title: EA Masters: Vote now for your favourite property industry supplier
item.author: Nadya Putri Maharani
item.description:
By Nadya Putri Maharani

The UK property industry’s most trusted suppliers are set to be honoured as voting opens for the 2026 Best EA Supplier Awards. This prestigious event, part of the EA Masters ceremony, will take place on 3 November at Evolution London. Estate agents nationwide can now rate their suppliers on a scale of one to 10, recognising those who have made a significant impact on their businesses.

Celebrating Excellence in the Property Industry

The Best EA Supplier Awards aim to shine a spotlight on the companies that support estate agents across the UK. Suppliers will be judged across three categories: Small, Medium, and Large, with Gold, Silver, and Bronze awards up for grabs in each. The Gold winners from these categories will then compete for the coveted title of Best EA Supplier of the Year. Last year’s winners, including Street Group, Dawsons Training, and Home Box Move, demonstrated the high standards of service that suppliers can achieve.

Heather Staff, co-founder of Street Group, expressed her gratitude for last year’s win, stating: “We measure our success by the success of our customers. Being recognised by the industry and voted for by agents, whilst seeing our clients win awards themselves, truly means the world to us.”

How the Awards Benefit the Industry

The awards not only celebrate outstanding suppliers but also provide a valuable benchmark for the property industry. Through the EA Masters ratings system, the top 10% of suppliers will receive an Excellent rating, while the top 5% will earn the Exceptional title. This independent feedback helps estate agents make informed decisions when choosing suppliers, fostering a culture of excellence and accountability.

Estate agents are encouraged to participate by casting their votes and leaving reviews for their suppliers. By doing so, they contribute to a transparent and collaborative industry environment. Voting is now open, and agents can submit their feedback here.

As the property industry continues to evolve, recognising the suppliers who drive its success remains crucial. The Best EA Supplier Awards offer a unique opportunity for estate agents to acknowledge the partners who help them thrive, whilst inspiring others to raise their standards. With voting underway, the countdown to this year’s ceremony has officially begun.

item.title: One month in, prime minister. Take the handbrake off, or watch Britain seize up
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
By Bambang Setiawan

As the new Prime Minister settles into their role, the property market remains in a state of stagnation, awaiting decisive action to reignite its momentum. Housing transactions are a cornerstone of the UK economy, yet recent data suggests a concerning slowdown. With no immediate plans to reform stamp duty and ongoing uncertainty around potential tax changes, the market continues to face significant challenges. Addressing these issues could be crucial for stimulating growth and restoring confidence among buyers, sellers, and industry professionals alike.

The Current State of the Housing Market

Recent figures from Connells Group highlight a worrying trend in the property market. The time taken to progress from a sale agreement to the exchange of contracts has increased significantly, now averaging 104 days compared to just 73 days a decade ago. For leasehold properties, this figure rises to 155 days, further complicating the process. Alarmingly, one in three transactions collapses before reaching completion, leaving both buyers and sellers frustrated.

In April, 61% of deals took longer to reach exchange than it did to secure a buyer in the first place. This inefficiency places immense pressure on estate agents, conveyancers, and mortgage brokers, who are forced to navigate outdated and cumbersome processes. While the industry demonstrated its ability to accelerate transactions during the last stamp duty holiday, such urgency is absent in day-to-day operations. This raises questions about why, in an increasingly digital age, the property market remains burdened by antiquated procedures.

Challenges at Both Ends of the Market

The housing market faces two distinct yet interconnected challenges. In the second-hand property sector, supply is at a 12-year high, but many homes remain unsold due to a mismatch between sellers’ expectations and buyers’ willingness to pay. This pricing issue often leads to prolonged marketing periods and eventual price reductions. Estate agents play a pivotal role here, encouraging realistic valuations to facilitate quicker sales and keep the market moving.

Conversely, the new-build sector is grappling with a shortage of available properties. Fewer planning permissions and delays in construction have exacerbated the supply gap, leaving buyers with limited options. This imbalance underscores the need for a coordinated approach to address both ends of the market, ensuring that supply meets demand and transactions proceed more smoothly.

As the government considers its next steps, prioritising reforms to streamline the property transaction process and stimulate activity could prove vital. By tackling inefficiencies and fostering a more dynamic market, policymakers have the opportunity to unlock the housing sector’s potential as a driver of economic growth.

item.title: Estate agents feel the heat as property market cools
item.author: Nadya Putri Maharani
item.description:
By Nadya Putri Maharani

The UK property market is experiencing a seasonal slowdown, with estate agents reporting weaker-than-usual activity this summer. According to a recent survey commissioned by GetAgent, 78% of estate agents anticipate a quieter period compared to typical summer levels. Whilst summer holidays traditionally see a dip in market activity, prolonged hot weather this year appears to have exacerbated the trend.

Summer Holidays and Hot Weather Impact Market Activity

The school holidays often lead to a reduction in both buyer and seller activity, and this year is no exception. Nearly two-thirds (64%) of estate agents noted that seller activity usually declines during this period, with 45% reporting a significant drop. Buyer demand follows a similar pattern, with 58% of agents stating they typically receive fewer enquiries during the summer break. Of these, 27% described the reduction as substantial.

However, this summer’s prolonged hot weather has added further pressure to the market. An overwhelming 91% of agents reported that the heat has reduced activity in their local markets, with 55% describing the impact as significant. Property viewings appear to have been most affected, cited by 53% of respondents, followed by buyer enquiries (28%) and seller enquiries (19%).

Estate Agents Face Increased Workloads Despite Slowdown

Whilst fewer buyers and sellers are entering the market, estate agents’ workloads have not necessarily decreased. In fact, 74% of agents said they remain as busy as usual or even busier, as they focus on progressing existing transactions towards exchange and completion. This period also coincides with staff holidays, which can add to the pressure. Around 45% of agents reported that annual leave makes workloads harder to manage during the summer, with 27% stating that reduced staffing has a significant impact on operational efficiency.

Colby Short, co-founder and CEO of GetAgent, commented: “Summer has always brought a natural lull to the property market as families head away and attention turns to the school holidays. The prolonged hot weather we’ve experienced this year seems to be adding another layer to that seasonal slowdown, particularly when it comes to viewings and the level of buyer activity we’re seeing across the market.”

As the property market navigates this seasonal dip, estate agents are balancing the challenges of reduced activity with the demands of progressing existing transactions. Homeowners considering listing their property or buyers looking to move may wish to factor in these seasonal trends when planning their next steps.

item.title: The property market: should we all go over Beachy Head or is the cavalry coming to our rescue?
item.author: Rizky Aditya Pratama
item.description:
By Rizky Aditya Pratama

Recent developments in the UK property market have left many homeowners and potential buyers questioning what the future holds. With rising interest rates, increasing living costs, and a challenging economic landscape, some may feel uncertain about their next steps. However, understanding the current trends and exploring available options could help borrowers navigate these turbulent times.

Interest Rates and Mortgage Costs

One of the most pressing concerns for homeowners is the impact of rising interest rates on mortgage repayments. The Bank of England’s base rate has seen multiple increases over the past year, leading to higher borrowing costs for many. Those on variable-rate mortgages or nearing the end of fixed-term deals may find their monthly payments significantly higher. Borrowers might consider reviewing their mortgage arrangements, exploring remortgaging options, or seeking advice from a financial adviser to ensure they are on the most suitable deal.

The Housing Market Outlook

The UK housing market has experienced fluctuations in recent months, with some areas seeing price declines while others remain resilient. Factors such as inflation, energy costs, and broader economic uncertainty have contributed to this mixed picture. For those looking to buy, it could be worth researching local market conditions and being prepared for potential negotiation opportunities. Meanwhile, homeowners planning to sell may wish to ensure their property is competitively priced and presented to attract buyers in a slower market.

Government Support and Policy Changes

Government policies and initiatives can play a significant role in shaping the property market. Recent discussions around welfare reform, energy bill support, and housing supply have sparked debate about the long-term solutions needed to address affordability and accessibility. Whilst immediate relief measures, such as VAT reductions on energy bills, may offer some respite, broader structural changes could be required to stabilise the market. Borrowers and homeowners may wish to stay informed about policy developments that could impact their financial planning.

Navigating the current property market landscape may feel daunting, but staying informed and proactive can help homeowners and buyers make confident decisions. Whether it’s reviewing mortgage options, monitoring market trends, or keeping an eye on policy changes, taking steps to understand the situation could provide clarity during uncertain times.

item.title: Property industry leaders join forces to tackle transaction delays
item.author: Sri Wahyuni Astuti
item.description:
By Sri Wahyuni Astuti

Property industry leaders have come together to form an advisory board aimed at tackling lengthy transaction times and reducing fall-through rates in the UK housing market. Spearheaded by BestAgent founder Charlie Lamdin, the board includes prominent figures from estate agency, conveyancing, and property technology sectors. Among the members are Yopa CEO Verona Frankish, Thomas Legal and Equilaw Group CEO Simon David, and DDRE Global founder Daniel Daggers. Rory Sutherland, president emeritus of Ogilvy Consulting, also joins as both an adviser and investor in BestAgent.

The initiative follows growing concerns over the efficiency and reliability of residential property transactions. According to the government’s Home Buying and Selling Reform Roadmap, published in June, the average transaction now takes approximately 120 days from offer acceptance to completion—significantly longer than in 2007. Additionally, around one in three transactions fails to reach completion, causing frustration for buyers and sellers alike.

Addressing the Challenges

The advisory board will support BestAgent in its mission to streamline the home-moving process, with a focus on halving transaction times and reducing fall-through rates. Lamdin highlights that delays often stem from misaligned incentives across the housing market, where estate agents compete for instructions, portals prioritise advertising, and professionals focus on isolated aspects of the process. By prioritising transparency and completed transactions, BestAgent aims to create a more cohesive and efficient system.

One of the company’s key strategies is its Find Your Agent service, which allows prospective sellers to invite local estate agents to pitch for their business. Sellers can watch short videos from participating agents before selecting individuals to visit their property for valuations and further discussions. Importantly, agents cannot pay for preferential positioning within the service, and only the agent ultimately chosen by the seller incurs a charge. This approach aims to level the playing field, giving independent agencies a fairer chance to compete against larger corporate businesses.

A Collaborative Approach

The board’s diverse expertise underscores the importance of collaboration in addressing systemic issues within the property market. Alongside industry leaders, the group includes Alex Groundwater, a former programme director at FT, Sony, Cisco, and Crown Estate; property acquisition specialist Jo Henry; Animos founder Andrew Tillard; and retired Charles Russell Speechly partner Nick Armstrong. Together, they will advise BestAgent as it refines its proposition and works towards its ambitious targets.

Lamdin emphasises that the UK is not lacking in property websites or estate agents but rather in completed moves. By fostering greater transparency and efficiency, BestAgent hopes to transform the home-moving experience for buyers and sellers across the country.

As the property market continues to evolve, initiatives like this could play a crucial role in reducing delays and improving outcomes for all parties involved. Homeowners looking to sell or buy may wish to explore services such as Find Your Agent to streamline their journey and make informed decisions.

item.title: Property investment firm acquires estate agency network with 104 franchisees
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
By Bambang Setiawan

Property investment specialist Sourced has expanded its operations into estate agency services following the acquisition of Open House Estate Agents. The deal adds 104 franchisees to Sourced's existing network of over 230 operators, while allowing Open House to maintain its current brand and business model.

Expanding property services

The acquisition brings together two Warrington-based property businesses with similar approaches to franchising. Both companies combine local operators with centralised technology and support systems. For Sourced, the move represents a strategic expansion from its core services in property investment, finance and lettings into residential sales and auctions.

Open House franchisees will gain access to Sourced's existing infrastructure, including an acquisition funding programme that could help them purchase letting agencies or property portfolios. The combined network now covers the full property transaction process - from investment and finance through to sales, lettings, auctions and management.

Shared business philosophy

Stephen Moss, head of Sourced, highlighted the alignment between the two companies: "What stood out was how closely Open House's approach matched our own. Both networks support ambitious local operators with the systems and opportunities of a national organisation."

Rather than making immediate changes, Sourced plans to focus on identifying synergies between the two networks. Moss emphasised: "We're not looking to alter what makes Open House successful - we want to build on it." The estate agency brings established sales and auctions expertise to the group, while Sourced can offer its wider property network and technology to Open House franchisees.

For property professionals considering franchise opportunities, the merger creates one of the UK's largest networks with over 330 operators nationwide. The combined resources could provide franchisees with enhanced support and growth potential across multiple property sectors.

item.title: Landlords in rent arrears hit record low
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
By Bambang Setiawan

New research indicates that UK landlords are experiencing fewer rent arrears than ever before, alongside improving profitability across the private rental sector. The findings from Pegasus Insight suggest the buy-to-let market may be showing signs of stabilisation after recent economic challenges.

Record low arrears signal tenant resilience

The latest data reveals the proportion of landlords facing rental payment delays has fallen to its lowest level since records began. This improvement comes despite ongoing cost-of-living pressures, suggesting many tenants are prioritising rent payments even as household budgets remain tight.

Several factors may be contributing to this trend:

  • Strong employment figures maintaining tenant incomes
  • More landlords implementing thorough affordability checks
  • Increased use of rent payment technology reducing administrative delays

Rental yields remain healthy for investors

Alongside the reduction in arrears, the research highlights continued healthy yields across most UK regions. Rental demand continues to outstrip supply in many areas, allowing landlords to maintain competitive returns on their investments.

item.title: North offers better returns over five years
item.author: Nadya Putri Maharani
item.description:
By Nadya Putri Maharani

New research highlights a striking financial divide between property ownership in the North of England and renting in London, with homeowners in Newcastle potentially £100,000 better off over five years compared to tenants in the capital. The findings from Tembo suggest regional property markets continue to offer markedly different outcomes for residents and investors alike.

The North-South property divide

Analysis of housing costs reveals how geographical choices impact long-term finances. Whilst London remains the UK's most expensive rental market, northern cities like Newcastle present more affordable entry points for buyers. Over a five-year period, the combined effects of mortgage repayments, equity growth and rental savings appear to create significant advantages for northern homeowners.

The £100,000 differential accounts for:

  • Lower property purchase prices in Newcastle compared to London
  • Mortgage payments contributing to equity rather than rental costs
  • Potential capital growth on owned properties
  • Absence of annual rental increases typically seen in the capital

Regional considerations for buyers

Prospective homeowners might weigh several factors when comparing locations:

  • Northern cities often offer higher rental yields for investors
  • Commuter towns near major northern cities provide balance between affordability and employment opportunities
  • Government schemes like Help to Buy may stretch further outside London
  • Ongoing regeneration projects in northern cities could support future price growth

Whilst the figures present a compelling case for northern property investment, personal circumstances including employment, family ties and lifestyle preferences will always play crucial roles in relocation decisions. Mortgage applicants may wish to consult independent financial advisers to assess how regional property markets align with their long-term plans.

As the UK housing market continues to evolve, these findings underscore the importance of location in financial planning, with northern cities demonstrating particular value for both homeowners and property investors.

item.title: Commuter house price growth highest for Glasgow and Manchester
item.author: Rizky Aditya Pratama
item.description:
By Rizky Aditya Pratama

Recent research from Rightmove highlights significant disparities in house price growth across key commuter cities in the UK. Glasgow and Manchester have emerged as frontrunners, with both cities experiencing robust increases in property values compared to other urban travel hubs. This trend underscores the shifting dynamics of the property market as buyers continue to prioritise affordability and connectivity.

Glasgow and Manchester lead the way

According to Rightmove’s data, Glasgow and Manchester have seen the strongest house price growth among commuter cities. This surge reflects the increasing demand for homes in areas that offer a balance between urban amenities and accessibility. Both cities have become hotspots for buyers seeking value for money, particularly amidst rising interest rates and the cost-of-living crisis.

Manchester, in particular, has benefited from its thriving economy and extensive transport links, making it an attractive option for professionals commuting to nearby cities like Liverpool and Leeds. Meanwhile, Glasgow’s appeal lies in its cultural vibrancy and relatively lower property prices compared to other major UK cities.

Contrasting trends across the UK

While Glasgow and Manchester have experienced notable growth, other commuter cities have seen more modest increases. London’s commuter belt, for instance, has shown slower price growth, likely due to the capital’s already high property costs. Similarly, cities in the South East have faced challenges as buyers seek more affordable alternatives further north.

This divergence highlights the importance of regional factors in shaping property market trends. Factors such as local employment opportunities, transport infrastructure, and housing supply all play a role in determining where prices rise fastest.

What does this mean for buyers and investors?

For prospective buyers, the growth in Glasgow and Manchester could present opportunities to invest in areas with strong potential for capital appreciation. However, it’s essential to consider all aspects of a property purchase, including mortgage affordability and long-term financial goals.

Investors might also find value in exploring these markets, particularly if they are looking for rental properties. The demand for housing in these cities, coupled with their economic resilience, could make them appealing options for buy-to-let portfolios.

As the property market continues to evolve, keeping an eye on regional trends could help buyers and investors make informed decisions. Glasgow and Manchester’s recent performance serves as a reminder of the importance of location in achieving both short-term gains and long-term stability.

item.title: Central London office space under offer hits 19-year high
item.author: Sri Wahyuni Astuti
item.description:
By Sri Wahyuni Astuti

Central London's commercial property market has reached a notable milestone, with the volume of office space under offer hitting its highest level in nearly two decades. Recent data reveals particularly strong demand for premium Grade A offices, driven by major corporate occupiers seeking high-quality workspace in the capital.

Surge in leasing activity across prime locations

The past quarter has seen a dramatic acceleration in commercial leasing deals across central London's business districts. Key areas including the City, Canary Wharf and the West End have all reported significant increases in pre-let agreements and office space reservations. Market analysts suggest this reflects growing business confidence and a clear preference for modern, sustainable workspaces amongst corporate tenants.

Several factors appear to be driving this trend:

  • Major financial and professional services firms securing long-term premises
  • Increased demand for buildings with strong sustainability credentials
  • Flight to quality as companies prioritise employee wellbeing features

Grade A properties dominate the market

The current demand surge centres on Grade A office space, which typically offers the latest amenities, energy-efficient designs and prime locations. Commercial property experts note these premium buildings now account for over 70% of all central London office deals currently under offer.

Commercial property investors might consider these market conditions particularly favourable for landlords with high-specification developments. The imbalance between supply and demand for top-tier offices could potentially support continued rental growth in central London's core business districts.

While the commercial sector shows strong momentum, market watchers will be monitoring whether this positive trend continues throughout the remainder of the year. The current activity levels suggest many businesses remain committed to maintaining a physical presence in London, albeit in workspaces that meet modern environmental and employee expectations.

item.title: Automation becoming essential to residential letting
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
By Bambang Setiawan

The private rental sector is undergoing a digital transformation, with automation tools becoming indispensable for modern letting agents and property managers. As tenant expectations evolve and operational demands increase, technology is reshaping how landlords manage their portfolios efficiently.

Why automation matters in lettings

Property professionals are increasingly turning to automated solutions to streamline repetitive tasks and improve service quality. Key areas where technology is making an impact include:

  • Automated tenant referencing and background checks
  • Digital contract signing and document management
  • Smart rent collection systems with payment reminders
  • AI-powered maintenance request triaging
  • Automated communications for viewings and inspections

These innovations can help reduce administrative burdens whilst maintaining compliance with ever-changing regulations. For landlords with multiple properties, automation tools may prove particularly valuable in scaling operations without proportionally increasing management costs.

Balancing technology with personal service

Whilst automation offers clear efficiency benefits, successful letting agents are finding ways to blend technology with human expertise. Many renters still value personal interactions for complex queries or sensitive matters. Property professionals might consider:

  • Using chatbots for routine enquiries while maintaining phone support
  • Implementing automated viewings alongside traditional accompanied visits
  • Combining digital rent collection with personal payment plan discussions when needed

The most effective strategies often involve using automation to handle repetitive tasks, freeing up staff time for higher-value activities that require human judgement and empathy.

As the lettings landscape becomes more technologically advanced, both landlords and tenants stand to benefit from improved efficiency and transparency. However, the human element remains crucial in building trust and managing the more nuanced aspects of tenancy relationships.

item.title: Living in Accra, Ghana: Where to Begin
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
Exploring Property Investment Opportunities in Ghana

By Bambang Setiawan

Ghana's capital city of Accra has emerged as an increasingly attractive location for property investors looking beyond traditional UK markets. With West Africa enjoying a period of relative economic stability, and Ghana receiving substantial international support for development initiatives, the country presents some interesting opportunities for those considering overseas property investments.

The World Bank's ongoing support for Ghana's Second Resilient and Development Policy Operation aims to strengthen several key sectors that could benefit property investors. These include financial sector growth, energy sector improvements and climate resilience projects - all factors that contribute to creating a more stable environment for property investment.

Key Considerations for UK Investors

For UK-based investors exploring Accra's property market, several factors may warrant careful consideration. The city offers a growing middle class and increasing demand for quality housing, particularly in areas like Airport Residential, Cantonments and East Legon. However, overseas investors might want to thoroughly research local property laws, taxation systems and currency regulations before committing.

Mortgage options for foreign buyers in Ghana differ significantly from UK products, with local banks typically offering shorter loan terms and higher interest rates. Some investors opt to purchase properties outright or explore developer financing options. It could be worth consulting with both UK-based international mortgage specialists and local Ghanaian legal experts to understand all financial implications.

Balancing Potential and Practicalities

While Ghana's economic prospects appear promising, property investors should carefully weigh potential returns against practical challenges. The country's property market lacks the regulatory framework and transparency of more established markets, meaning thorough due diligence becomes even more crucial. Factors like reliable title deeds, construction quality and local infrastructure should all form part of any investment decision.

For those considering a move to Accra rather than purely investment purposes, rental yields in prime areas can be attractive, though tenants typically expect fully furnished properties with amenities. The expatriate community remains relatively small but well-established, with international schools and healthcare facilities available.

As with any overseas property venture, UK investors might want to proceed cautiously, starting with thorough research and potentially short-term visits before making long-term commitments. Ghana's property market shows interesting potential, but requires careful navigation to identify genuine opportunities.

item.title: How to Choose a Dependable London Removal Company
item.author: Nadya Putri Maharani
item.description:
By Nadya Putri Maharani

Moving home in London presents unique challenges that make choosing a reliable removal company crucial. Whilst opting for the cheapest quote might seem tempting, homeowners may find that cutting corners on removals can lead to costly delays, damaged belongings and unnecessary stress. With narrow staircases, parking restrictions and unpredictable lift access across the capital, selecting a specialist London removals firm could make all the difference to a smooth relocation.

Why Cheap Quotes Can Prove Costly

Many Londoners have experienced the nightmare scenario of furniture wedged in stairwells or removal vans stuck in pedestrian zones. The capital’s unique infrastructure means that removal companies require specific expertise to navigate:

  • Historic buildings with restricted access
  • Congestion charge zones and parking limitations
  • Time-sensitive moves within short rental periods

Bargain removal services often cut costs by using inexperienced staff, inadequate insurance or unsuitable vehicles. Homeowners might consider that paying slightly more for a reputable firm could ultimately save money by preventing damage to property or belongings.

Key Considerations When Choosing a London Removals Company

When evaluating removal firms in the capital, there are several factors worth prioritising:

  • London-specific experience: Look for companies with extensive knowledge of different boroughs and property types
  • Insurance coverage: Ensure the firm provides adequate protection for high-value items
  • Customer reviews: Check independent platforms for feedback about punctuality and care
  • Specialist equipment: Confirm availability of items like piano trolleys or carpet protectors

Many reliable removal companies offer free in-person surveys to assess the job properly rather than providing estimates over the phone. This allows for more accurate quotes and helps identify potential challenges in advance.

Planning for a Stress-Free London Move

Beyond selecting the right company, homeowners might consider these additional tips for smoother London relocations:

  • Book removals well in advance, especially for summer moves
  • Check parking bay suspension rules with the local council
  • Prepare an essentials box with items needed immediately
  • Label boxes clearly by room to speed up unloading

Whilst moving home in London will always involve some complexity, choosing an experienced removal company with local knowledge could significantly reduce stress. Investing in professional help may prove more cost-effective than dealing with the fallout from a botched DIY move or unreliable service.

item.title: What Smaller Energy Providers Offer That the Big Six Simply Don’t
item.author: Rizky Aditya Pratama
item.description:
By Rizky Aditya Pratama

In recent years, the energy market in the UK has undergone a significant transformation. Whilst the Big Six energy providers once dominated the landscape, a growing number of smaller, fully licensed suppliers have entered the fray. These emerging companies are offering competitive alternatives, often challenging the established giants on price, customer service, and sustainability. For homeowners looking to reduce their energy bills or align with greener options, exploring these smaller providers could be worthwhile.

Competitive Pricing

One of the most appealing aspects of smaller energy providers is their ability to offer competitive pricing. With lower overheads and more streamlined operations, these companies often pass savings directly to their customers. This can result in lower tariffs compared to those offered by the Big Six. Consumers who regularly compare energy deals may find that switching to a smaller provider helps them secure a more cost-effective solution without compromising on service quality.

Personalised Customer Service

Smaller energy providers frequently pride themselves on delivering a more personalised customer experience. Unlike larger companies, which may handle millions of accounts, smaller suppliers often have fewer customers, allowing them to focus on individual needs. This can translate to quicker response times, more tailored support, and a greater willingness to resolve issues efficiently. For homeowners who value responsive and attentive service, smaller providers might be an attractive option.

Commitment to Green Energy

Another area where smaller energy providers are making strides is in their commitment to renewable energy. Many of these companies prioritise sustainability, offering tariffs that source electricity from wind, solar, and other renewable sources. This focus on green energy appeals to environmentally conscious consumers who wish to reduce their carbon footprint. Whilst the Big Six also offer renewable energy options, smaller providers often lead the way in innovation and transparency when it comes to sustainable practices.

As the energy market continues to evolve, homeowners have more choices than ever before. Whilst the Big Six remain a reliable option for many, exploring the offerings of smaller providers could uncover benefits such as lower costs, improved customer service, and greener energy solutions. Regularly reviewing energy deals and considering alternative suppliers may help households find the best fit for their needs.

item.title: How to Choose a Dependable London Removal Company
item.author: Sri Wahyuni Astuti
item.description:
By Sri Wahyuni Astuti

Moving home in London can be a stressful experience, particularly when relying on removal companies that may not deliver as promised. Whilst budget options might seem appealing initially, homeowners may find that cutting corners could lead to costly delays or damaged belongings. Choosing a dependable removals service requires careful consideration of several key factors.

Researching Removal Companies

Londoners might consider starting their search by checking online reviews and testimonials from previous customers. Trusted review platforms can provide insight into a company’s reliability, punctuality and handling of fragile items. It could also be worth verifying whether the firm is a member of the British Association of Removers (BAR), as this indicates adherence to industry standards.

Other aspects to research include:

  • Insurance coverage for belongings during transit
  • Transparent pricing with no hidden fees
  • Availability of packing services if required
  • Experience with properties similar to the one being moved from or to

Getting Accurate Quotes

When requesting quotes, homeowners may wish to provide as much detail as possible about their move. This includes the volume of items, any specialist furniture or valuables, and access considerations at both properties. Reputable companies will typically conduct an in-person or video survey before providing a final price, rather than offering vague estimates.

Whilst cost is an important factor, the cheapest option may not always represent the best value. Borrowers might consider balancing affordability with service quality, as rushed or under-resourced moves could result in additional expenses later, such as replacement costs for damaged goods.

Taking the time to select a trustworthy removals company could help ensure a smoother transition to a new home. Comparing multiple options and checking credentials may provide peace of mind during what is often one of life’s more challenging events.

item.title: 7 Benefits of Installing a Composite Door
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
By Bambang Setiawan

For homeowners looking to upgrade their property’s entrance, composite doors offer a modern alternative to traditional timber or uPVC options. Combining multiple materials into one durable design, these doors have become increasingly popular for their blend of security, aesthetics, and energy efficiency. But what exactly makes them stand out?

What Are Composite Doors?

Unlike single-material doors, composite doors are constructed using layered components. A typical design might feature a solid timber or foam core for stability, wrapped in a glass-reinforced plastic (GRP) exterior for weather resistance. Additional materials are often incorporated to enhance insulation and structural integrity. This multi-layered approach creates a door that performs well across multiple key areas.

Key Advantages of Composite Doors

Homeowners considering a front door replacement might find several compelling reasons to choose composite:

  • Enhanced security – The robust construction makes forced entry significantly more difficult compared to standard doors, with many models meeting Secured by Design standards.

item.title: Prime property network rebrands after listings near £4bn
item.author: Bambang Setiawan
item.description:
By Bambang Setiawan

The exclusive property network Oskar has unveiled a new identity as Oskar Prime, marking its expansion across the UK’s high-end residential market. The rebrand follows significant growth, with nearly £4bn of premium properties now listed on its private platform.

A growing network for prime property professionals

Since launching in early 2024, Oskar Prime has attracted 479 agents from 229 firms to its membership-based platform. The service facilitates discreet property sharing between estate agents, buying agents and mortgage brokers, specialising in homes valued at £2m or more. Current figures show £3.97bn in listed properties and £3.12bn in active buyer searches circulating through the system.

Founder Caspar Harvard-Walls, a former buying agent, developed the platform to create a more collaborative environment for high-end property professionals. What began with a focus on prime central London has now expanded to serve the broader premium and super-prime markets across the country.

Discreet deals in the digital age

The rebrand to Oskar Prime reflects the platform’s evolution into a comprehensive digital hub for off-market transactions. Many luxury properties never appear on public portals, while serious buyers often prefer to keep their searches confidential. The network provides a secure space for professionals to match these discreet requirements without public exposure.

Harvard-Walls commented: “Prime property has always depended on professional relationships. Our platform modernises the traditional agent-to-agent network while maintaining the privacy the sector requires.” He added that reaching £4bn in listings represented a major milestone for the business, demonstrating strong demand for private property sharing solutions.

Membership remains free for qualified professionals, with the company emphasising its commitment to fostering collaboration rather than charging subscription fees. For high-net-worth individuals and their representatives, such networks can provide access to opportunities that might otherwise remain hidden from view.

As the premium property market continues to evolve, digital platforms like Oskar Prime are becoming increasingly important for connecting buyers, sellers and their professional advisors in an increasingly competitive landscape.

item.title: Landlord possession claims rise 6% as repossessions fall
item.author: Nadya Putri Maharani
item.description:
By Nadya Putri Maharani

New government figures reveal a mixed picture for the UK rental market, with landlord possession claims rising whilst actual repossessions decline. Ministry of Justice data for Q2 2026 shows a 6% annual increase in possession claims, reaching 23,635 cases between April and June. However, completed repossessions by bailiffs fell by 3% to 6,560 during the same period.

Diverging trends in the rental sector

The statistics highlight contrasting movements across different stages of the possession process. Whilst claims increased, the number of warrants issued fell by 6% and possession orders remained stable. Accelerated possession claims saw the most significant jump, rising 16% year-on-year.

Private landlords initiated 5% more claims compared to Q2 2025, accounting for 32% of the total. Social landlords brought 3% fewer cases, representing an equal share. Accelerated procedures made up 36% of all claims, suggesting landlords may be favouring this faster route where available.

These figures cover the initial period following the implementation of the Renters' Rights Act on 1 May. The Ministry of Justice has cautioned against attributing these trends directly to the new legislation, stating it will continue monitoring the situation.

Regional variations and processing times

London accounted for a disproportionate share of possession activity, handling 33% of all claims despite representing a smaller portion of the national rental market. The capital saw 7,793 claims - a 2% annual increase - and 31% of all possession orders. However, London's landlord warrants fell sharply by 20%, contributing to the national decline.

Processing times showed modest improvements for rental cases, with the median duration from claim to repossession shortening to 27.1 weeks (from 27.9 weeks in Q2 2025). Claims typically took 7.6 weeks to reach an order and 14.9 weeks to progress to a warrant.

Mortgage possession cases told a different story, with all stages showing significant reductions. Claims fell 20%, orders declined 17%, and warrants dropped 18%. Completed mortgage repossessions decreased by 14% to 1,008. Despite fewer cases, mortgage possession timelines extended considerably, reaching 49.1 weeks from claim to repossession - the longest duration since late 2023.

These figures suggest lenders may be exercising greater forbearance with struggling borrowers, whilst landlords appear more proactive in initiating proceedings even if fewer cases reach the repossession stage. Homeowners and landlords alike may wish to stay informed about these evolving trends in the property market.

item.title: Mayors could get powers to override councils on property developments
item.author: Rizky Aditya Pratama
item.description:
By Rizky Aditya Pratama

New proposals could see England’s regional mayors gain significant powers to influence local planning decisions, potentially reshaping how major property developments are approved. The suggested changes would allow mayors to intervene in council-level planning applications, either granting or refusing permission for large-scale housing and commercial projects. This shift aims to accelerate development in areas where it supports economic growth or helps meet national housing targets.

How the proposed powers could work

Under the plans, mayors would be able to "call in" planning applications for schemes meeting specific thresholds: residential developments of 150+ homes, commercial projects exceeding 15,000 square metres, or buildings taller than 30 metres. The measures would effectively bypass traditional local authority decision-making processes in certain cases, with mayors able to grant upfront permission without standard planning applications.

Ten of England’s 14 devolved mayors have reportedly expressed support for the proposals, which would align their planning powers more closely with those currently held by the Mayor of London. The government suggests these changes could help deliver its target of 1.5 million new homes during this parliamentary term while ensuring developments align with broader regional strategies.

Balancing local concerns with regional priorities

Proponents argue the measures could prevent important developments being blocked unnecessarily, whilst also providing a mechanism to stop inappropriate schemes that might otherwise gain local council approval. The powers would require mayors to consider existing planning rules and local plans, with ministers retaining ultimate oversight.

The proposals also include provisions for mayors to influence how national housing funding is allocated within their regions and to levy development contributions for infrastructure projects. However, critics have raised concerns about reduced local accountability, suggesting the changes might marginalise councillors, MPs and community voices in the planning process.

As the debate continues, homeowners and prospective buyers may wish to monitor how these potential changes could affect housing supply and development patterns in their regions. The proposals represent a significant potential shift in how England’s planning system balances local decision-making with regional strategic priorities.
